Petitioner
 Versus
The State of Jharkhand ..... ...

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi For the Petitioner :Mr. Rahul
Ranjan, Advocate For the State : Mr. Navin Kumar Gaunjhu, A.P.P. 02/ 05.12.2025:

Heard learned
counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2.  The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Ahilyapur P.S. Case No.47 of 2023,
for the alleged offences registered under Sections 411, 414, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120(B) and 34 of Indian Penal Code, Section 66(B), 66(C) and 66(D) of I.T. Act, pending in the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II-cum-Special Judge (Cyber Crime), Giridih.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has earlier moved before this Court in ABA No.3598 of 2024 which was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 15.04.2025.
He submits that thereafter another co-accused arising out of the same FIR in identical situation has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in ABA No.2660 of 2025 and another co-accused has been granted anticipatory bail in A.B.A. No. 5074 of 2025 and in view of that petitioner may kindly be granted anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-II-cum-Special Judge (Cyber Crime), Giridih
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel appearing for the State opposes the prayer and submits that earlier the petition was dismissed as withdrawn and in view of that the anticipatory bail of the petitioner may kindly be dismissed.

5. It is an admitted position that the petitioner has earlier moved ( 2025:JHHC:36477 ) before this Court in ABA No.3598 of 2024 which has been dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 15.04.2025 and thereafter another co-accused persons have been granted anticipatory bail by order dated Raju Mandal vs The State Of Jharkhand ..... ... ... on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148064351/

entities.text: Raju Mandal vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 08.08.2025 and by order dated 08.09.2025 in such circumstance the second anticipatory bail can be maintained and there are general and omnibus allegations against the petitioner and the name of the petitioner has come on the confessional statement, I am inclined to provide anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

6. Accordingly, the petitioner, above named, is hereby directed to surrender before the learned Court within three weeks from today, and in the event of his surrender/arrest, the petitioner, above named, shall be released on bail, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand), with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II-cum-Special Judge (Cyber Crime), Giridih in connection with Ahilyapur P.S. Case No.47 of 2023, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 482(2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

Dt.05.12.2025 ( Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.)
